stem.text: Water is pumped into a storage tank at a rate modeled by the differentiable function \( W \), where \( W(t) \) is measured in gallons per hour and \( t \) is measured in hours for \( 0 \le t \le 12 \). Selected values of \( W(t) \) are given in the table. \( \begin{array}{c|cccc} t \text{ (hours)} & 0 & 3 & 7 & 12 \\ \hline W(t) \text{ (gallons per hour)} & 20 & 26 & 35 & 41 \end{array} \)

parts.prompt: Use a left Riemann sum with the three subintervals indicated by the table to approximate \( \int_{0}^{12} W(t)\,dt \). Show the computations that lead to your answer.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval uses the rate at its left endpoint times its width.

points.criterion: Writes a left Riemann sum whose three terms each show a width and a rate value, 3(20) + 4(26) + 5(35), with at least five of the six factors correct, as the setup for the integral from 0 to 12.
Gives the value 339 with the supporting products present.

parts.prompt: Using correct units, explain the meaning of \( \int_{0}^{12} W(t)\,dt \) in the context of the problem.
parts.answer_latex: \text{total gallons pumped into the tank from } t = 0 \text{ to } t = 12

worked_solution.text: The integral of a rate over an interval is the amount accumulated over that interval.
worked_solution.latex: \int_{0}^{12} W(t)\,dt = \text{gallons of water pumped in during } 0 \le t \le 12

points.criterion: States that the integral is the total amount of water, in gallons, pumped into the tank over the time interval from t = 0 to t = 12 hours; both the quantity with gallons and the interval are needed.
